__comment: LOCAL smoke-test inputs, for miniwdl/Cromwell on your own machine. Sequence/GWAS input files are not committed (gitignored, and specific to whatever panel you are analysing) — point these at your own phylogeny, Rtab, and phenotype file before running.
__comment_covariates: covariates_file: sample_id plus one named column per covariate (e.g. RST, OspC, MLST, BAPS). covariate_combinations runs one pyseer call per entry - a bare name is a single-covariate run, '+' joins several into one joint run (e.g. 'RST+OspC'). Deliberately NOT all four at once here: RST/OspC/MLST/BAPS are categorical typing labels (never add a 'q' suffix to them, even though some are stored as integers), and MLST's high cardinality relative to a typical isolate panel makes an all-four joint run a real degrees-of-freedom risk, not just a style choice - see the pyseer_gwas README for a measured example.
__comment_lineage: lineage_clusters is optional; a BAPS export (sample_id\tBAPS) makes a ready-made --lineage-clusters file.
__comment_annotation: annotation_table is optional; Panaroo's gene_presence_absence.csv (not the .Rtab) or an equivalent module-annotation table.
